VoiceCommand.title: VoiceCommand
VoiceCommand.description: Represents a voice command received from the user.

id.description: Unique identifier for the voice command.

timestamp.description: Timestamp of when the voice command was received.

rawText.description: The raw text transcribed from the voice command.

interpretedText.description: The interpreted text of the voice command after processing by the AI.

commandType.description: The type of command (e.g., INSTALL, EXECUTE, MODIFY).

CommandExecution.title: CommandExecution
CommandExecution.description: Represents the execution of a command in Termux.

id.description: Unique identifier for the command execution.

executionTimestamp.description: Timestamp of when the command was executed.

command.description: The actual command that was executed.

exitCode.description: The exit code of the command execution.

output.description: The output of the command execution.

isSuccessful.description: Indicates whether the command execution was successful.

Installation.title: Installation
Installation.description: Represents an installation managed by the tool.

installationTimestamp.description: Timestamp of when the installation was initiated.

packageName.description: The name of the package being installed.

version.description: The version of the package being installed.

source.description: The source of the package (e.g., apt, git).

isSuccessful.description: Indicates whether the installation was successful.

CodeModification.title: CodeModification
CodeModification.description: Represents a code modification performed by the tool.

id.description: Unique identifier for the code modification.

modificationTimestamp.description: Timestamp of when the code modification was performed.

filePath.description: The path to the file that was modified.

description.description: A description of the code modification.

isSuccessful.description: Indicates whether the code modification was successful.

GithubIntegration.title: GithubIntegration
GithubIntegration.description: Represents an action performed involving Github, such as pulling and installing scripts.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Github Integration action.

actionTimestamp.description: Timestamp of when the GitHub action was performed.

repositoryUrl.description: The URL of the GitHub repository.

commitHash.description: The commit hash of the code that was pulled.

isSuccessful.description: Indicates whether the GitHub action was successful.

User.title: User
User.description: Represents a user of the application.

AIGuidance.title: AIGuidance
AIGuidance.description: Represents a guidance or suggestion provided by the AI to the user.

id.description: Unique identifier for the AI guidance.

timestamp.description: Timestamp of when the AI guidance was provided.

message.description: The message provided by the AI.

firestore.reasoning:
The Firestore structure is designed to ensure Authorization Independence, DBAC, and QAPs. User-owned data is stored under `/users/{userId}`. VoiceCommands and related entities (CommandExecution, Installation, CodeModification, GithubIntegration, AIGuidance) are stored as subcollections to the corresponding voice command, enabling efficient querying and organization. This also ensures that all data related to a user is grouped under their respective user document. Given that all data is directly tied to a user, there's no need for complex role-based access control, as access is determined by the user's ID.

Authorization Independence is achieved by denormalization. Specifically, the `userId` field is included in `VoiceCommand` documents. This ensures that access control rules can be applied to `voiceCommands` and subcollections without needing to perform `get()` operations on parent documents. This eliminates hierarchical authorization dependencies.

The structure supports QAPs by segregating data based on ownership. All data under `/users/{userId}` is owned by the user identified by `{userId}`, allowing for secure list operations based on the `request.auth.uid`. There are no collections mixing data with different access needs.
